fieldEvidence.excerpt: ADM reported on April 14, 2026 that the national H2CanFly consortium chose YMX Innovation to establish ARCTIC, a state-of-the-art centre for research on hydrogen as a clean propulsion technology.

ADM reported that Airbus is partnering with YMX Innovation to establish Protospace for experimentation, productivity, and training, alongside an automated drone-surveillance project at the Mirabel site.
Espace Aéro describes YMX Innovation Centre as owned and overseen by Aéroports de Montréal, located at the heart of the YMX International Aerocity, and a structuring project in the Mirabel hub.
Espace Aéro lists advanced air mobility, decarbonization, Industry 4.0 advanced manufacturing, and academic and professional training as YMX Innovation Centre sectors.
The City of Mirabel reports that the April 14, 2026 strategic advanced-air-mobility workshop was held at Centre YMX Innovation and informed a Quebec roadmap discussion.

DND states that NEXUS operates primarily from YMX Innovation Centre in Mirabel with secure collaboration spaces, specialized testing infrastructure, and regulated airspace for advanced experimentation and demonstrations.
The French DND release likewise places the CNACU primarily at Centre d'innovation YMX and describes secure collaboration spaces, specialized testing infrastructure, and regulated airspace.

DND identifies an Espace Aéro-led consortium and CJFC-sponsored NEXUS operating from YMX, while Espace Aéro describes YMX as the ADM-owned facility context; the record boundary remains a reviewer question.
ADM's April 2026 release describes seven operational strategic programs at YMX, including robotics, advanced air mobility, sustainable energy, and aerospace experimentation and training.
